data.title: JPM Foresees XIAOMI-W 3Q Adj. NP to Dive 58%; Smartphone Demand Still Weak
data.description:
JPMorgan released a research report forecasting that XIAOMI-W 's adjusted net profit for 3Q will shrink 58% YoY. The broker forecast AI investment to drive operating expenses above expectations, partly offset by growth in smartphone revenue and stabilizing gross margin.

It lowered its 3Q net profit forecast by 15%, estimating smartphone margins will trend toward stability, although demand is expected to remain weak. JPMorgan maintained a Neutral rating with a TP of HKD32.

The broker said smartphone shipments have recorded both QoQ and YoY declines for four straight quarters. It forecasts full-year shipments this year to fall 24% YoY, with declines expected to continue in 1H27 before a mild recovery possibly emerges in 2H27 at the earliest.

For AIoT, the broker predicted IoT revenue to decline 10% YoY in 2026, representing the largest drop among all segments, followed by another 3% decline in 2027.

In the EV segment, October deliveries crossed 50,000 units, with SkyNomad accounting for more than half. JPMorgan forecast deliveries of 450,000 units in 2026 and 650,000 units in 2027, below market expectations of 700,000-800,000 units. Expansion into Europe in 2H27 could be a potential positive catalyst, although regulatory restrictions in 2028 may limit upside potential.

data.title: Rupee climbs past 93/USD as investors seek shelter in Indian stocks, shorts unwind
data.description:
Key points:
  • Rupee trims 2026 losses to 3.5% from nearly 8% in May
  • Bankers say hedge funds unwound bearish rupee wagers this week
  • Overseas investors pour more than $12 billion into Indian stocks so far in November

By Jaspreet Kalra

The Indian rupee strengthened past the psychologically important 93-per-dollar mark on Friday for the first time since April, as Indian equities attracted investors fleeing AI-driven markets and oil prices dropped, accelerating a sharp reversal in the currency's fortunes.

The rupee has struggled for most of 2026, threatening to breach record low levels as recently as last month. It has since recovered sharply, cutting year-to-date losses to about 3% compared to nearly 8% at its weakest point in May and closing the week at 92.67, following its strongest session since October 12.

Friday's gains accompanied gains in Indian stocks in the face of a worsening global rout in AI-linked stocks. Asian shares logged their worst week since 2020. India's benchmark Nifty 50 , on the other hand, notched a fourth straight weekly gain.

Foreigners have poured $12 billion into Indian shares so far in November, the largest-ever monthly inflow, compared with more than $60 billion of selling from September 2024 to October 2026.

"More balanced global investor positioning and moderation in the oil price could see a sharp reversal in investor flows, to the benefit of the Indian stock market," said Edward Evans, portfolio manager at Ashmore Group.

The surge in inflows has sharply increased the supply of dollars, boosting the rupee at a time when measures taken by the Reserve Bank of India have curbed demand.

Earlier this year, policymakers rolled out steps to alleviate sustained pressure on the local currency, including clamping down on speculative trades, attracting capital inflows from overseas Indians and shifting crude oil import-related dollar demand out of the spot market.

As the rupee struggled near record low levels of 97 last month, RBI chief Sanjay Malhotra had hinted that monetary tightening could also be used to support the unit.

A sustained recovery may help reverse capital outflow-induced weakness in the currency, which has eroded returns for foreign investors and could deter further investments, analysts say.

OFFSHORE SHORTS UNWIND, EXPORTERS EYED

The rupee has also benefited from a rush to unwind bearish wagers on the currency this week, with the flows concentrated in offshore markets, bankers said.

The reversal, which four bankers said was led by overseas hedge funds, has been aggressive enough to lift the rupee to a rare premium in the non-deliverable forward markets.

The sentiment shift is also apparent in the options market, with a key gauge showing that demand for options betting on rupee weakness has eased relative to those betting on its strength.

"Importantly, the RBI is choosing to let the INR appreciate and not draw a floor by buying reserves to elicit a behavioural or expectation shift among exporters and offshore participants," said Dhiraj Nim, an economist and FX Strategist at ANZ.

Persistently elevated demand for forward dollars — typically from importers — has been a sore spot for the rupee throughout this year.

A reduction in speculative dollar demand from companies and an unwinding of offshore wagers are both helping the rupee, according to an FX salesperson at a foreign bank.

data.title: Eurozone Wage Growth Accelerates, But Remains Modest
data.description:
By Paul Hannon

Eurozone wage growth accelerated slightly in the three months through September, but remained modest despite the pickup in inflation triggered by the war between the U.S. and Iran.

The European Central Bank on Friday said wages negotiated by labor unions and similar groups were 2.57% higher in the third quarter than a year earlier, an increase in the annual rate of growth from 2.45% in the three months through June.

Since the start of the war, officials at the ECB have highlighted the outcome of wage negotiations as a key indicator as to whether the jump in energy prices triggered by the conflict is set to keep inflation above their 2% target.

But there are few signs as yet that workers are securing larger pay rises to cover increased energy bills.

"What we don't see at the moment is second-round effects, not yet," Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin said in an interview with CNBC Thursday. "We need to be vigilant about what will happen and that's the reason we've increased rates in the past."

The ECB raised its key rate in September and June.

data.title: India's OIS curve inverts at key tenors for first time in 18 months
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

India's overnight index swap curve has inverted at its most actively traded tenors for the first time in about 18 months, as heavy receiving pushed five-year rates below one-year rates, which remain elevated on rate hike concerns and high rupee forward premiums.

Here are a few details:

  • India's one-year OIS rate (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) stood at 6.48%, while the five-year rate (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) slipped to 6.46%.

  • The curve has inverted at these two key tenors for the first time since May 2025, when the RBI was in the middle of a rate-easing cycle.

  • Tanay Dalal, SVP, business and economic research at Axis Bank, said the inversion likely reflects global curve flattening during the AI-related selloff, along with elevated rupee forward premia.

  • A one-year rate above the five-year rate suggests the market expects aggressive near-term tightening, followed by stable or lower rates over the longer term.

  • The one-year OIS is pricing in roughly 75–100 bps of rate hikes, along with tight liquidity and high forward premium.

  • Far-forward USD/INR premium have risen, with the implied yield at 4.30%, and traders are watching the RBI and Fed rate paths.

  • Recent declines in oil prices and US Treasury yields are also pulling the five-year OIS rate lower.

data.title: Wall Street Wrap: ASTS, BE, MDB Stocks Win Bullish Calls As PEP, USAR, SMMT Face Downgrades
data.description:
Key points:
  • B. Riley upgraded AST SpaceMobile to Buy with a $48 target, saying fears are priced in.
  • BMO moved Bloom Energy to Outperform, citing projects that are showing real execution.
  • Bernstein cut PepsiCo and Summit Therapeutics to Underperform.

Wall Street analysts were split sharply this week, upgrading AST SpaceMobile (ASTS), Bloom Energy (BE) and MongoDB (MDB) on a better risk-reward setup and AI demand, while downgrading PepsiCo (PEP), USA Rare Earth (USAR) and Summit Therapeutics (SMMT) over earnings pressure in North America, feedstock shortages and clinical and regulatory execution concerns.

AST SpaceMobile, Bloom Energy Upgraded On Growth Catalysts 

B. Riley upgraded AST SpaceMobile to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ with a $48 price target. The firm argues that worries about capital commitments and constellation deployment are already priced into the shares. So are newer concerns about the rocket development partnership with Firefly Aerospace (FLY). The analyst thinks investors are overlooking what a successful rocket program could deliver, along with other catalysts.

BMO Capital took a similar step on Bloom Energy, moving it to ‘Outperform’ from ‘Market Perform’. The price target fell to $230 from $260. BMO had been cautious, questioning the company’s large-scale proof of concept, whether a higher-cost power solution holds up once grid availability improves, and its dependence on U.S. data center demand.

Those debates haven’t gone away. But shares have pulled back, and large projects, including Nebius, are now supplying the execution evidence BMO wanted. Risk-reward has become more attractive, the firm said.

UBS Turns Bullish On MongoDB, Sees AI Workloads Driving Growth 

UBS raised MongoDB’s rating to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ and increased its price target to $450 from $375. ‘It expects MongoDB to handle 20% to 40% of new AI workloads, potentially helping revenue growth exceed 20%.

BofA kept its ‘Buy’ rating but cut its target to $450 from $540 ahead of fiscal third-quarter results on December 1.

Analysts Flag Near-Term Challenges For PepsiCo And USA Rare Earth

Bernstein analyst Cristian Rios downgraded PepsiCo to ‘Underperform’ from ‘Market Perform’ and trimmed the price target to $128 from $131. He expects the company to miss earnings expectations over the next 12 months, driven by weakness in North America.

William Blair’s Neal Dingmann downgraded USA Rare Earth to ‘Market Perform’ from ‘Outperform’ and dropped the price target. He said the company is putting the pieces together for notable future upside. But feedstock shortages add to a growing list of near-term problems.

The shortages are hurting Less Common Metals and, in turn, the Stillwater magnet plant. For now, William Blair prefers companies with a longer track record of processing material.

Bernstein Downgrades SMMT Over Drug Development Missteps

Bernstein analyst Jeffrey Walch downgraded Summit Therapeutics to ‘Underperform’ from ‘Market Perform’ and cut the price target to $8.30 from $11.90. The firm now has doubts about Summit’s drug development capabilities. It pointed to at least three mistakes in how the company handled its recent HARMONi interaction with the FDA.

Too many trial results came from China; Summit analyzed the data too early four times, and it did not clearly explain regional approval risks.

data.title: Lufthansa to Cut 1,000 Jobs at Flagship Airline as Challenges Mount
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Deutsche Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 jobs at its flagship airline, as surging fuel prices add to challenges the unit is facing in its efforts to revive its fortunes.

Lufthansa Airlines informed employees about a series of measures to deepen its turnaround, including a plan to cut a total of 1,000 full-time positions at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, according to a letter seen by Dow Jones Newswires.

As of the end of 2025, the German carrier group had 103,255 employees worldwide, with 64% of them employed at passenger airlines, according to Lufthansa's latest annual report. In addition to its namesake carrier, the company also owns Swiss Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines and Eurowings.

"Over the past weeks and months, we have talked about and discussed the challenging financial situation at Lufthansa Airlines extensively. Unfortunately, the situation has not improved," the letter said.

The airline plans additional reductions to its short- and medium-haul capacity and to accelerate the rollout of SpaceX's Starlink across its fleet in a bid to generate additional revenue by commercializing internet access, according to the letter.

The performance of Lufthansa's flagship airline has weighed on the results of the overall group this year, with the company calling out in third-quarter results earlier this month hits from rising fuel costs and expenses tied to strikes that hurt its profitability.

Carsten Spohr, Deutsche Lufthansa's chief executive, said earlier this month that the group's core brand needed to accelerate its financial turnaround through both previously planned and additional measures.

data.title: HSFO crack holds at more than four-month low
data.description:
The crack for high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) extended declines at the Asia close on Friday, hovering at over a four-month low as expectations of more supplies continued to weigh on sentiment.

The 380-cst HSFO/Brent December crack (FO380BRTCKMc1) closed at a discount near $6.35 a barrel on Friday, LSEG data showed, last lower in early July. Meanwhile, cash differentials for HSFO steadied on Friday after the previous session's slump.

Apart from stronger Middle Eastern supplies expected, regional supplies in Asia also held steady, according to market sources. India's HPCL offered an HSFO cargo for Mumbai loading over December 5-7 via a tender that closed on Friday.

Meanwhile, China's fuel oil import demand showed signs of ticking up in recent weeks, according to ship-tracking data. Fuel oil imports firmed for a third consecutive week into November, Kpler data showed.

Latest customs data from China released on Friday showed that October imports had recovered to a seven-month high, totalling 1.95 million tons.

As for very low-sulphur fuel oil (VLSFO), the market firmed slightly on Friday amid a firmer premium traded, though the product crack (LFO05SGBRTCMc1) eased to a premium near $19 a barrel.

INVENTORY DATA

- Fuel oil inventories in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp hub (STK-FO-ARA) rose 8.8% to 1.06 million tons in the week to November 19, recovering to a high last seen before the Iran war, Dutch consultancy Insights Global data showed.

OTHER NEWS

- Oil prices edged down on Friday and were set for a weekly decline on strong exports from the Middle East despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

- China's crude oil imports from its biggest supplier Russia were 10.03 million metric tons in October, or 2.36 million barrels per day, up 10% year-on-year, according to customs data published on Friday.

- Indian refiners' crude throughput rose nearly 2% from September to 5.70 million barrels per day (24.11 million metric tons) in October, provisional government data showed.

- Russia's crude oil output risks falling again as Ukrainian attacks on refineries and export infrastructure intensify, analysts and traders say.
